ui_bugs.issue: SHIPPED WITH SYNTAX/REFERENCE BUG. The useEffect line was concatenated with a stray fragment 'api.get(`/creditcards/${id}/transactions`)...' that references an undefined `id`. Result: navigating to /credit-cards crashed the entire app with 'ReferenceError: id is not defined', un-mounting the sidebar and blocking every subsequent nav (accounts, poonji, profit, reports, settings). Fixed by extracting into a proper `loadTxns(id)` helper that matches the loadTxns(c.id) call site on line 61.

rca of the issue: CreditCards.jsx crash: during the iteration-2 refactor to support ?new=1 auto-open modals, the ?new=1 useEffect was appended on the same line as a leftover `api.get(`/creditcards/${id}/transactions`)...` fragment that used to be the body of a `loadTxns(id)` helper. The wrapping `const loadTxns = (id) => { ... }` was lost, leaving a bare expression referencing an out-of-scope `id`. React renders the component -> the bare expression executes -> ReferenceError. Because there is no ErrorBoundary, the whole Layout unmounts. Reproduction: log in with any valid user, click sidebar 'Credit Cards' -> app becomes blank with an overlay 'Uncaught runtime errors: id is not defined at CreditCards'. Mitigation applied: re-wrapped the fragment into `const loadTxns = (id) => { api.get(...).then(...).catch(...); };` on a separate line. Verified by re-navigating all 13 sidebar items with 0 pageerrors.
